s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital syndrome with cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Left proptosis with resistance to globe retropulsion
Left superior orbit mass extending to the cavernous sinus
key_facts: 2-month history of diplopia and pain
Recurring forehead lesion first excised 6 years prior to presentation
Initial histopathologic findings showed Breslow thickness of 6 mm and 14 mitotic figures/mm2
Extensive perineural and intraneural invasion
Lesion recurred twice
Visual acuity 20/20 bilaterally without afferent pupillary defect
Left upper eyelid edema, erythema, and ptosis
Limited adduction on the left with associated strabismus
Forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve
MRI finding of left superior orbit mass with indistinct borders and fat stranding
Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with associated fat stranding

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial histopathologic findings and recurrence with perineural invasion

shortlist.label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive perineural and intraneural invasion, and cranial nerve involvement

shortlist.label: Desmoplastic melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring forehead lesion with histopathologic findings of melanoma and perineural invasion

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible origin from skin lesion with perineural invasion

shortlist.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Perineural invasion and cranial nerve involvement, although less likely than melanoma

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a recurring forehead lesion with initial histopathologic findings showing a Breslow thickness of 6 mm, 14 mitotic figures/mm2, and extensive perineural and intraneural invasion, combined with the MRI finding of a left superior orbit mass and the pathological examination showing malignant cells with mitotic activity in the nerve, strongly supports the diagnosis of malignant melanoma.

rejected.label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
rejected.why: While perineural invasion is present, the primary lesion is described as a forehead lesion with histopathologic findings consistent with melanoma, not a nerve sheath tumor.

rejected.label: Desmoplastic melanoma
rejected.why: Although desmoplastic melanoma can have perineural invasion, the provided histopathologic details and imaging findings do not specifically suggest this subtype over conventional malignant melanoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of histopathologic findings typical for squamous cell carcinoma, such as keratinization or intercellular bridges, and the clinical presentation does not align closely with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
rejected.why: The histopathologic and imaging findings do not support adenoid cystic carcinoma, which typically arises from salivary glands and has distinct histological features not described in this case.
